problem: Robot navigation from natural-language commands admits many valid paths, and existing systems use a fixed default navigation style, so users must repeatedly issue corrections and clarifications to adapt the robot to their personal preferences.
motivation: Robot teammates need to be reliable and predictable to be trusted. Instructing a robot at every step burdens users, while fully independent robots are unpredictable. Learning per-user preferences from ongoing dialogue could make collaborative exploration faster and reduce clarification commands.
key_idea: Use preference-based reinforcement learning, with spoken user corrections treated as negative reward and acceptance as positive reward, to select the end waypoint of a navigation command that each user prefers, inserted into an ASR/NLP-to-ROS pipeline.
insight: This is a work-in-progress proposal with no experiments or ablations, so no empirical insight is given. The argued rationale is that relative (preference) feedback avoids hand-set numeric rewards, and reducing navigation to end waypoints (pose plus surrounding-space features) should reduce training needs. A key open problem is telling implicit corrections from moving on to the next subtask.
method: Feedback as reward: user speech is converted to text and classified as correction/clarification (negative reward) or acceptance (positive reward), restricted to unambiguous phrasing such as 'No, robot do X' and 'Yes, robot do Y next'.
Preference-based RL formulation: an MDP with Preference (S,A,mu,delta,gamma,rho), learning from pairwise trajectory preferences instead of absolute rewards.

Waypoint representation: each of eight instruction types (e.g., approach an entrance, enter an unexplored room) maps to a final ROS pose (3D point plus quaternion). Only the end location is learned, not the path.
State features: robot position and orientation, plus features of the surrounding space such as visibility and free room (e.g., facing a wall <1 ft away versus open space).

Message bridge integration: pipeline of push-to-talk mic, ASR, NLP intent classifier, ROS message bridge, robot. The preference module is inserted as the penultimate stage to choose the user-preferred trajectory among those the instruction allows. The bridge is bidirectional with text-to-speech.
Planned evaluation: simulated exploration task in ROS/Gazebo with LIDAR and RGB camera. Metrics are task completion, time, and number of verbal corrections, plus post-interaction surveys.

setting.backbone: Preference-based RL agent (planned; details not finalized), with ASR + NLP intent classifier front end
setting.training_data: Planned online learning from per-user dialogue feedback in simulation; builds on previously collected human-robot dialogue data; no training reported
setting.observation: LIDAR scans and RGB camera on a simulated ground robot; pose and surrounding-space features
setting.action_space: Predicted end waypoints (ROS poses: 3D position + quaternion); path execution delegated to motion planning
setting.privileged: Predefined waypoints as landmarks (landmark resolution assumed)

numbers_note: Work-in-progress position paper; no experimental results reported.
results: No results are reported; the paper describes the planned approach and evaluation. The hypothesis is that preference-adapted navigation will shorten task time and reduce clarification commands.
limitations: No implementation or experiments yet; algorithm training details are unfinished.
Assumes predefined waypoints/landmarks and restricts feedback to explicit unambiguous language, so implicit feedback is not handled.
Only end waypoints are learned (not paths), and testing is in simulation only.
builds_on: Wizard-of-Oz human-robot dialogue experiments (Marge et al.)
